featured_reviews.review_text:
Very weird and extremely disappointing experience. I ordered Singapore Chicken Fried Rice but it honestly felt like I had ordered sweet coconut rice instead. The rice was dry, had a strange sweet taste, and there was almost no chicken in it. The appearance of the food was also very odd. It only had a few onions and green capsicum pieces and even those looked strange and not fresh.

I had to eat it with difficulty because I did not have time to return it or raise a complaint at that moment.

This is not the first issue I have faced with this restaurant. The last time I ordered Paneer Fried Rice and tea, but the tea was missing from my order. When I called the restaurant, they told me they would add it in my next order if I reminded them. Obviously, no one places another order just to claim one tea that was already paid for.

I also tried for a long time to connect with Zomato support and even that experience was frustrating. After multiple attempts the call finally connected and I did receive my refund, but the overall experience was still very poor.

After a long time I decided to order again because this item was showing as highly reordered and recommended on the app. The price was ₹240 and I used a discount coupon to get it for a lower price. But using a discount coupon does NOT mean the restaurant can pack anything they want or compromise with food quality and quantity.

There was also no option for half or full portion, so I expected proper quantity and standard quality. The delivery itself took almost one hour, so clearly the food was not prepared in a hurry. That makes it even more shocking that such poor quality food was delivered.

I did not even click any pictures because the experience itself was enough to regret ordering.

During the Ramadan month people order food with trust, especially for iftar. Facing such poor quality food during this time is extremely disappointing and unacceptable.

Zomato seriously needs to take action against restaurants that send such poor quality food to customers. Platforms should not just show “highly recommended” or “most reordered” tags if the actual food quality is this bad. Customers trust these ratings and spend their money based on them.

Because of this experience I will avoid ordering from this restaurant again and I will not recommend it to anyone. Ratings might look good on the platform, but in reality the service and food quality felt worse than zero.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Some places feed you. Jewel feeds your soul.
If you've lived in Powai even for a month and haven't found yourself at Jewel Fast Food at midnight, hunched over a steaming plate of momos or wrapping your hands around one of their legendary cups of chai — have you even really lived here?
This place is the definition of a legacy joint. No gimmicks, no Instagram lighting, no fancy rebrand. Just honest, soul-warming food that has kept this neighbourhood running for years. The chai alone is worth the trip — thick, perfectly spiced, and served with the kind of confidence that only comes from years of getting it absolutely right.
The Chinese is proper street-style comfort food — saucy, flavourful, and never lets you down. And the momos? Plump, juicy, piping hot. Exactly what you need after a long day or a late night out.
And speaking of late nights — open till 3 AM. In a city that never truly sleeps, Jewel is there when every other option has packed up and gone home. Hungry after a party? Late shift at work? Just restless and craving something warm at 1 AM? Jewel's got you. Every single time.
This isn't just a food joint. It's a Powai institution. The kind of place that shows up in college memories, late-night conversations, and "remember when we used to go to—" stories years later.
If you haven't been — go tonight. And if you have been, you already know. 🙏

featured_reviews.name: Kumar Dave
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Prasad Food Divine, Powai, Mumbai, for dinner with my family after reading several positive reviews and noticing its fine-dining positioning. Unfortunately, our experience did not live up to the expectations.

The food was just average—neither bad nor exceptional. While the menu offers a good variety of options, the taste did not justify the premium pricing. Service was another area of concern; it was noticeably slow throughout our visit.

One surprising disappointment was that cold mineral water bottles were not available when requested, which is quite unexpected for a restaurant that presents itself as a fine-dining establishment.

Another major concern was the ambiance. During our dinner, there were two birthday celebrations with loud recorded songs and significant noise levels. While celebrations are understandable, a fine-dining restaurant is generally expected to provide a calm, comfortable, and relatively private dining atmosphere. The excessive noise disturbed the overall experience and made it difficult to enjoy a relaxed family dinner.

Overall, the ambiance is decent, but considering the food quality, service, noise levels, and pricing, we did not find good value for money. Based on our experience, the restaurant did not meet the expectations associated with a fine-dining destination. Hoping the management addresses these concerns and improves the overall guest experience.

Our inaugural visit to Lake View Café was, regrettably, underwhelming despite its promising premise.

The buffet boasted an impressively expansive spread, encompassing Southeast Asian, Indian, and continental cuisines, reflecting commendable variety and ambition. However, the execution fell short of expectation, with the offerings lacking any discernible “wow” factor.

A particularly notable drawback was the quality of the chicken across several dishes, which appeared less than fresh and was consistently tough, detracting significantly from the dining experience. Even relatively straightforward preparations, such as the pasta, required multiple iterations before reaching an acceptable standard—an avoidable lapse in a setting of this calibre.

Service, too, proved to be disappointingly pedestrian, falling well below the benchmark set by establishments such as JW Marriott Mumbai and Taj Mahal Palace.

In sum, while the breadth of the spread is undeniably impressive, the inconsistency in execution and lacklustre service rendered the experience far from memorable.

featured_reviews.name: Patricia
featured_reviews.review_text: I decided to head here for an afternoon lunch with a few friends on a weekend. This place had a lot of good reviews and was hoping to have some good food. However we were a bit disappointed. The place was huge and had a lovely ambience. The staff was courteous and they had live music which was a tad bit too loud because we had to scream over each other to be heard. For food we got the sassy chicken 65 and the grilled chicken flatbread which was good and so we thought the other things would be good too. But we got the crispy lotis stem next which lacked flavour and the rawa fried prawns which came with a weird sauce which seemed rather stale. We then ordered desserts hoping this would save the day but the desserts were pretty mediocre. We got the salted caramel cheesecake which tastes like a peda more than a cake and the chocolate seven ways which was mostly three ways. They did however not charge us for the cheesecake after we complained.

featured_reviews.name: rahul gupta
featured_reviews.review_text:
Sassy Spoon is a delightful restaurant that offers a fantastic dining experience. I recently visited and was thoroughly impressed by the quality of food and the overall ambiance. The tacos I ordered were absolutely delicious — well-seasoned, perfectly cooked, and presented beautifully. It’s clear that a lot of thought goes into their food preparation and presentation.

The restaurant has a cozy yet vibrant atmosphere, making it a great place to unwind with friends or enjoy a casual meal. The interiors are tastefully done, creating a pleasant and inviting environment. The background music was subtle and didn’t overpower conversations, which added to the charm.

Located in a prime area, Sassy Spoon is easy to find and accessible. The staff was courteous, attentive, and prompt in their service, ensuring we had a comfortable experience throughout. The menu has a wide variety of options, and the pricing felt reasonable for the quality offered.

Whether you’re a foodie or someone just looking for a relaxed outing, Sassy Spoon won’t disappoint. I would highly recommend trying their tacos and exploring other items on the menu — it’s definitely a place worth revisiting. Overall, a great spot for good food, good vibes, and a memorable time.

featured_reviews.review_text:
the service seemed a bit off this visit, the food: k-pop chicken wings were so good, the grilled chicken in bbq flatbread and the crispy chicken tenders was mid.

featured_reviews.review_text: Beautiful ambience. Staff was polite, good service. Lesser quantity at this price point. I like spicy food so I don't like food much. However, 10/10 for ambience and service. Good place to hangout and parties.

featured_reviews.name: Girish Kumar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Please allow me to explain the reason for my rating.

We visited the place after one of my friend at college got placed with a good company.
We reach the restaurant around 10, and we were rushed into ordering soon as the kitchen was closing soon which is understandable.
We ordered pork ribs, Punjabi mutton curry, Spaghetti and a couple of starters.
The first thing that shocked us was the portion size, the atrociously priced started just had 4 pieces, and the main course was half the size of a usual main course.
The taste was also sub-par, and when we asked for the manager, they stalled us for half an hour and then they tell us that the manager is on leave, and then we asked for a feedback book, after which they again stalled for another half an hour and then they come back empty handed and they tell us they don't have a feedback book.
That's just sad for a restaurant it's size.

The ambience was good but I was expecting better hospitality and better tasting food.

featured_reviews.name: Vighnesh Joshi
featured_reviews.review_text:
My visit to The Sassy Spoon was for a very short time but I will definitely visit again and again.
The ambience is beautiful.
In salad we ordered Warm lemony couscous with toasted almonds & grilled chicken which was the best salad I ever had.
In small plates we had Apple wood smoked beetroot & goat cheese croquettes with tomato chilli jam which tasted sweet and savoury and really good in taste.
Also we had Grilled chicken in house smoked BBQ glaze, mozzarella & fresh basil.

Overall it was a wonderful experience at The Sassy Spoon.
Kudos to all the staff for amazing service.
